exampleDiffers.scope: The answer carries the scopes associated with the grant refreshed (the page: "the response contains the new access token, refresh token, and scopes associated with the new grant"): this grant is the one TwitchDev authorized above, channel:moderate, chat:edit and chat:read; the page's example refreshed a grant of two other scopes.
exampleDiffers.expires_in: A user access token lasts about four hours; the page's 15583 is its own token's lifetime and the code example's 14124 the twin's.

exampleDiffers.data[].content_classification_labels: The channel holds the labels its broadcaster set (Gambling added, DrugsIntoxication removed, the step before). notReplayed.oauth2Token#doc Device code grant flow:: The device code grant is the twin's gap: no demanded app and no step of the life starts a device flow (POST /oauth2/device is not served), so the token endpoint answers this grant as the twin answers what it does not serve.
notReplayed.modifyChannelInformation#doc Modify Chan: The page publishes this body with typographic quotes and // comments, so it is not JSON a client can send; what it does (labels added and removed, is_branded_content) is replayed from the request body table as "content classification labels added and removed".
notReplayed.getStreams#doc Get Streams: Gets informa: A stream exists only while a broadcaster's encoder publishes RTMP to the ingest (live media); no journey step speaks RTMP yet (the walk has no RTMP client), so no World a walk makes holds a live stream to list.
notReplayed.getStreams#doc Get Streams: Gets streams: As the list of the most active streams: a live stream is made only by an encoder's RTMP publish, which no journey step can make.
notReplayed.sendChatMessage#doc Send Chat Message: The example sets for_source_only, which "can only be set when utilizing an App Access Token" (its body table): the app access token path (a prior user:bot and channel:bot authorization) is the twin's gap, and no demanded caller sends chat with one.
